title: Geomorphic Evolution of the Lower Semliki River, Uganda: Bed and Bank Change, 2000–2026 (SFFS Technical Report SEM.9.7)

creators.name: Kakooza, Charles
creators.affiliation: Ministry of Water and Environment, Uganda

creators.name: Zaake, Benon
creators.affiliation: Ministry of Water and Environment, Uganda

description:
The lower Semliki — the 92 km of river between the Bweramule gauge and Lake Albert, and the 10 km above the gauge — is the reach that floods Ntoroko District, western Uganda. This technical report of the Semliki Flood Forecasting System (SFFS) measures how its banks and bed have changed since 2000, using 27 annual low-flow water masks from Landsat (2000–2026, 30 m) and 11 from Sentinel-2 (2016–2026, 10 m), 4,090 transects spaced 25 m apart, 139 bends, the 191 discharge gaugings made at Bweramule between 1950 and 2025, and water levels from 12 satellite-altimetry virtual stations. It maps erosion and deposition, gives retreat rates and 50-year setbacks for every bend, identifies the meander necks closest to cutting off, tests whether the bed has aggraded, and says what each finding means for the HEC-RAS model that forecasts the river level and for planning in the delta.

Key findings. The river is an active meander belt in its first 40 km below the gauge and nearly stable in its last 30 km: between 2000–04 and 2020–26, 265 ha of land became channel and 299 ha of channel became land. Outer banks retreat at 4.5–5.0 m a year at the typical bend in the first 40 km, about 1.5 m a year between km 40 and 60 and about 1 m a year beyond km 60; the fastest bends move 11–13 m a year. A 97 m neck at km 14.2 is the next cut-off, within roughly 3–10 years if present rates hold. The bed at the gauge shows no net aggradation in 70 years, though the control has drifted. Rising low water in the lower reach reflects the rise of Lake Albert, not sediment. A 50-year setback of about 205 m keeps half of the bends clear and about 580 m keeps nine in ten clear.

Contents. The report (PDF); the annual Landsat and Sentinel-2 channel-water masks and the transect, bend and neck results (zip); a Python module and four Jupyter notebooks that rebuild the masks in Google Earth Engine, re-run the transect analysis, the planform-change maps and the width series, and document the specific-gauge and altimetry methods. The discharge gaugings, gauge levels and hydraulic model of the Ministry of Water and Environment are not included; they are available from the Ministry on request. Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2016–2026); Landsat imagery courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey.
